allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

payload.statement_nl: Let A,B be integers with A >= B >= 0. For d=0 one has Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1, the weighted polynomial ring is S=Q, and the empty sequence of elements of S is a homogeneous regular sequence. Its quotient is S itself, whose graded Hilbert series is 1.

used_only_standard_definitions_implicit_: a weighted polynomial ring with 0 variables is Q
the ideal generated by the empty sequence is 0
Q is concentrated in degree 0, so its Hilbert series is 1

result_payload.proof_nl: Fix integers A,B with A>=B>=0. In the d-parameter construction under discussion, setting d=0 gives the boundary case where the defining product for Q_{A,B,d}(q) has no factors. Hence Q_{A,B,0}(q) is the empty product, so Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. Likewise, the weighted polynomial ring at parameter d has one variable for each index 1,...,d; when d=0 there are no variables, so the ring is just the coefficient field Q. Thus S=Q. Now consider the empty sequence in S. There are no elements to check, so the homogeneity condition is vacuous. The regularity condition is also vacuous; and if one includes the usual requirement that the final quotient be nonzero, that is satisfied as well because S=Q is nonzero. Therefore the empty sequence is a homogeneous regular sequence in S. The ideal generated by the empty sequence is the zero ideal, so the quotient by that sequence is S/(0)=S itself. Finally, with the induced grading on the zero-variable weighted polynomial ring S=Q, we have S_0=Q and S_m=0 for every m>0. Therefore the graded Hilbert series is H_S(t)=sum_{m>=0} dim_Q(S_m) t^m = 1. This proves all parts of the statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Specializing to d=0 gives an empty product, hence Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1; the weighted polynomial ring has zero variables, hence S=Q; the empty sequence is vacuously homogeneous and regular; its quotient is S itself; and since Q is concentrated in degree 0, its graded Hilbert series is 1.

used_external_facts: Standard conventions: an empty product equals 1; a polynomial ring over Q in 0 variables is Q; the empty sequence is a homogeneous regular sequence in a nonzero ring; the graded Hilbert series of Q concentrated in degree 0 is 1.
